error_analyses.observable_characteristics: The implemented focus order moves consecutively from the footer promo link (label 22) to a descendant button inside that same link (label 23). Navigation_order assigns consecutive meaningful positions 22 and 23, and the KFG visibleCtrlDomSequence also places them consecutively. The screenshot shows a dark footer promo area with a prominent LEARN MORE button inside the same promo block, followed by platform/app links. No supplied ground-truth transition is labeled as an LNF for this page.
error_analyses.matching_criteria: A reported LNF where the source and destination are parent/descendant interactive elements within the same visible promo/card region, the implemented tab sequence is consecutive in Stage 1/KFG, and there is no supplied reference LNF label for that transition.
error_analyses.possible_cause: Observed evidence shows a nested interactive relationship: the destination XPath is inside the source XPath. A plausible detector error is that the original detector treated focus entering a descendant interactive element inside an already focusable container/link as a linear-navigation failure or suspicious duplicate stop, even though the supplied reference data does not classify it as an LNF. Whether the underlying HTML pattern is invalid or confusing is separate from the LNF label and cannot be concluded here.

subject_summary: This subject contains one evaluated detector error and no ground-truth LNFs, so there are no FNs. The FP is a consecutive focus move within a footer promo block from a focusable link to a descendant button. Evidence supports a likely detector over-trigger on nested interactive structure rather than a documented WCAG 2.4.3 failure. Uncertainty remains only about the detector's internal rule, not about the observed implemented sequence.
